matches.quote: Several conclusions depend on this specific film being fully reduced, single-phase... - the 0.7 eV "RE peak"... The assignment of the 0.7 eV peak to Pr 5d... untested.
Uniqueness and comparability of the exchange constants. Five parameters (J1-J4, J⊥) are fitted to a single dispersion per compound... report the fit covariance
a dispersion consistent with LSW does not establish long-range 3D order... "Support a 3D antiferromagnetic order" should become "show three-dimensional spin correlations"
account for the near-Γ points in PrNiO2 lying within about 1.5-2 resolution widths of a very strong specular elastic line and a phonon... Show those fits
Fig. 2(a) is a sum over H = 0.4-0.475, which broadens a dispersing magnon. State whether the damping values in Fig. 3(b) come from individual spectra.
Better still, compare with Sr-doped infinite-layer nickelates (Ref. 12 and the authors' own Ref. 46), where the doping dependence of damping in the same material family is known.
The substrates differ (STO against NGO; a = 3.94 against 3.86 Å), so part of the factor of about two in J1 may reflect lattice parameter and strain
The elastic maximum near (0.2,0.2) and the extra elastic intensity beyond (0.25,0.25) are read as possible stripe order (p. 5)... this should be stated more cautiously.
account for the near-Γ points in PrNiO2 lying within about 1.5-2 resolution widths of a very strong specular elastic line and a phonon... with large error bars.
The fitting details (DHO convolution, which widths are fixed, how the phonon and RE components are constrained, and how the 95% intervals are computed) are needed to judge Figs. 3 and 5.
The crystal-field, spin-orbit, exchange-field and broadening parameters behind Fig. 4(g-l) are not given.
"a proof of the fully occurred topotactic reduction" (p. 5), which is circular... Ni L-edge XAS, which would expose residual Ni2+/Ni3+ or partly reduced regions.
Δ = 8 eV was "chosen sufficiently larger than U also providing reasonable results" (p. 7), which reads as tuning... U = 3.2 eV for Ni is far below... 5-7 eV

notes: P2 and P4 are section header artifacts. For C8, the review raises the exact mechanism (changing weights of overlapping non-dispersive components causing an apparent dispersion shift) for the dxy orbiton in P3, and asks to show the low-q magnon fits overlapping with the elastic and phonon peaks in P6. For C2 and C3, P8 and P18 question full reduction/absence of excess oxygen and whether the 0.7 eV peak is intrinsic or Pr 5d, without citing impurity XRD peaks or objecting to the phrase 'chemically undoped' specifically, so both are scored 'partly'.
